newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack at full output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack at full output.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Friday its 115,000 barrels a day Cossack offshore crude oil operation was operating at full capacity.
"Our current production is at full capacity. There is absolutely no constraint on production at the moment," Woodside spokesman Graeme Atherton told Reuters from Perth.
Atherton added that over the last week, production had been running up to 5,000 barrels in excess of design capacity.
He said the operation also was considering delaying maintenance work on the gas export system and an associated cut in production until October to avoid delaying shipments that already had been sold.

Production at Cossack is planned to be cut to 50,000 to 60,000 barrels of crude oil a day for three weeks to allow repairs to be carried out on a faulty key component of the gas export system which is causing accelerated wear on other parts.

"We were looking at doing that in September. However, because that would interrupt oil cargoes, we thought rather than cause inconvenience to customers at that point we would defer the work. We are now looking at an alternative time to do it, possibly in October," Atherton said.
But he noted that there would be a 24-hour full shutdown of the Cossack facility September 6 to do some repair work.
He said he was unaware of any existing or planned delays to shipments.
Gas reaches the Cossack Pioneer production vessel, is cooled and dehydrated and then sent into a pipeline to the North Rankin platform before heading onshore for refining production.

The gas dehydration system contains the faulty part, called a vapour knock-out drum, which removes free water from the gas. The wet gas passes from the drum through a molecular sieve dehydration unit designed to handle wet gas but not heavy water droplets. The vapour unit is not removing enough water.

"They're components that are designed to last for several years, we've had to replace them after six months of operation because they're handling much wetter gas than they are designed to," Atherton said.
He was unable to give normal gas production figures.
Equal partners in the field are Woodside, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd and units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
